Question: Would a one (1)-man crewed tank be feasible, and would it be more effective than a 3-4 person crewed tank?
Answer: Former tank gunner in a German Army armored reconnaissance unit here. To open the armored motor hatch of our light tank, you needed at least two strong people. The same goes for many other tasks that a tank crew has to accomplish: changing the tracks and cleaning the main cannon require more than one person. Of course, one could somehow automate this procedure but this would add a lot of additional weight to the vehicle. A tank crew member, on the other hand, is versatile and can do many different tasks. Where I see the main problem, however, is with problem-solving. Tanks break down all the time and get damaged, not only by enemy fire. What do you do when, during a firefight, you lose your radio communication or your hydraulics? The latter happened to us many times in training. In this case, we had two options: fix the problem or go manual (all vital systems of a tank can also be operated manually, with pedals and cranks). Good luck doing this without a second crew member! During a ride on a Ukrainian tank near the frontline. On some Russian/Soviet tank models, the loader has been replaced by an automated loading system. This feature has proven inferior to tank designs with a conventional manual loading system. (Picture by the author of this post) Your most important task is to shoot the enemy (tank) before they can shoot you. You need to be very fast and accurate. Of course, this can be automated but four eyes will always see more than two. The traditional commander/gunner team is a proven concept and highly superior to tanks where only one person conducts the fight. Last but not least, when the sh*t hits the fan, you want to have a human being next to you who pulls your wounded a** out of the burning tank and gives you first aid. I admit that at the beginning, I was a bit skeptical about spending money on something that is often used to create content for TikTok or Instagram, but there’s a lot soldiers can learn from these videos. Answer: Traveling in Eastern Ukraine isn’t safe for anyone. This is not only because of the fighting but there are some additional factors: A main road in the Donetsk region.
